Affiliation:: School of Computer Science, University of Oklahoma
Research Domains: Lightweight Model Design for Limited Data
Techniques Used: Lesion blob extraction and random redistribution
Seamless lesion projection onto disease-free images
Horizontal and vertical flipping of lesion masks
Two-way CNN combining U-Net with image classification
Parallel Morphological Operations (erosion, dilation, opening, closing, residual)
Gaussian weight initialization with binarization threshold
Statistical significance testing via 30-run Monte Carlo simulation
Dice score and Intersection over Union (IOU) metric analysis
Reduced convolution block size (32x32) for complexity reduction
Average pooling and linear layers for classification head
Data & Platforms: Clinic-provided healthy retinal fundus images (60 images)
Skin cancer dataset (1200 images with annotated lesion masks)
ORIGA-light dataset (Online Retinal Fundus Image Database for Glaucoma Analysis and Research)
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Synthetic Data Augmentation via Lesion Projection: Mitigating dataset scarcity and class imbalance by extracting pathological features from existing images and seamlessly projecting them onto healthy backgrounds to generate diverse training samples.

Joint Multi-Task Learning Architectures: Employing hybrid two-way CNNs (e.g., J-Net) that simultaneously perform semantic segmentation and disease classification to share encoder features and improve diagnostic robustness compared to independent models.

Hybrid Lightweight Model Optimization: Combining mathematical morphology operations with Extreme Learning Machines and Random Forest ensembles to create efficient, low-complexity models suitable for resource-constrained environments and small medical datasets.

Iterative Threshold Optimization and Validation: Enhancing classification precision through SoftMax threshold optimization, multi-seed Monte Carlo simulations, and incremental subset training to ensure statistical significance and reduce false positives in ambiguous cases.
Summary Description: Sanjana Mudduluru specializes in medical imaging informatics, developing robust deep learning frameworks for computer-aided diagnosis in ophthalmology and dermatology. Her research addresses critical challenges in medical AI, including data scarcity, class imbalance, and model overfitting. She pioneers synthetic data generation techniques, such as lesion blob projection, to enhance dataset diversity. Mudduluru designs novel joint multi-task architectures like J-Net for simultaneous segmentation and classification, and develops lightweight hybrid models combining morphological operations with ensemble classifiers for efficient glaucoma and melanoma detection. Her work emphasizes rigorous validation through Monte Carlo simulations and threshold optimization, delivering clinically relevant, high-accuracy diagnostic tools optimized for limited data environments.
